answer: All poultry (including breasts, whole birds, legs, thighs, wings, ground poultry, giblets, and stuffing) must be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165°F (73.9°C) [USDA FSIS Safe Temperature Chart | Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart | p.2] or 74°C (165°F) or above for less than 1 second (instantaneous) [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-401.11 | p.84].

Time/temperature control for safety food shall be maintained at 57°C (135°F) or above during hot holding, except for certain roasts that may be held at 54°C (130°F) or above [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-501.16 | p.93].
Time/temperature control for safety food must be maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less when cold holding. [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-501.16 | p.93]
Cooked food must be cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-501.14 | p.92].

Refrigerated ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held, or opened from a commercial container, may be kept for a maximum of 7 days at 41°F or less, counting the day of preparation or opening as Day 1. [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-501.17 | p.93]

answer: Cold time/temperature control for safety food must be maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-501.16 | p.93]. *Listeria* is hardy and tolerates cold temperatures unlike many other foodborne bacteria [FDA Bad Bug Book (2nd ed.) | Listeria monocytogenes | p.99], but the documents do not state whether it can still grow at 5°C (41°F).

Eggs must be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 160°F (71.1°C) [USDA FSIS Safe Temperature Chart | Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart | p.2], or 145°F (63°C) for 15 seconds for raw eggs broken and prepared in response to a consumer's order and for immediate service [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-401.11 | p.83]. 

The bacterium associated with eggs is *Salmonella* (such as *Salmonella Enteritidis*) [FDA Bad Bug Book (2nd ed.) | Salmonella species | p.12, 14].

Cooked time/temperature control for safety food must be cooled within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70°F), and within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41°F) or less [FDA Food Code 2022 | §3-501.14 | p.92]. When food cools too slowly, *Clostridium perfringens* is known for multiplying much faster than most other bacteria [FDA Bad Bug Book (2nd ed.) | Clostridium perfringens | p.82].

Fish and shellfish require a minimum internal temperature of 145 degrees F [USDA FSIS Safe Temperature Chart | Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart | p.2]. Raw oysters are linked to *Vibrio parahaemolyticus* [FDA Bad Bug Book (2nd ed.) | Vibrio parahaemolyticus | p.29] and *Vibrio vulnificus* [FDA Bad Bug Book (2nd ed.) | Vibrio vulnificus | p.45].

A food employee must be excluded from work if they are symptomatic with vomiting or diarrhea, jaundiced (with onset within the last 7 calendar days), diagnosed with an infection from Hepatitis A virus, or diagnosed with Typhoid fever [FDA Food Code 2022 | §2-201.12 | p.52]. 

Salmonella causes two kinds of illness: gastrointestinal illness (which causes nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, cramps, and fever) and typhoidal illness (which causes high fever, diarrhea or constipation, aches, headache, lethargy, and sometimes a rash) [FDA Bad Bug Book (2nd ed.) | Salmonella species | p.12].
